source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Vitamin D carrying fairly little relevance to the renal bone disease that develops as a complication of chronic kidney disease","B":"This medication being used mainly to treat an unrelated condition rather than the client's CKD-related mineral bone disease","C":"Impaired kidneys tending to produce an excess of active vitamin D rather than too little of it","D":"Impaired kidneys have reduced ability to activate vitamin D, so an active analog helps support calcium absorption and PTH regulation"}}
source_row.rationale: Impaired kidneys have reduced ability to convert vitamin D to its active form, so an active vitamin D analog like calcitriol helps support calcium absorption and appropriate PTH regulation, addressing CKD-related mineral and bone disease.
source_row.source_detail: Rationale for Active Vitamin D Analog Use in CKD
